episodes.175219: A large upper trough moved slowly through California on December 30 and 31. This system had a deep fetch of tropical moisture associated with it which resulted in a period of moderate to heavy precipitation along with widespread flooding across much of the area on December 31. Numerous reports of flooding and debris flows were reported by law enforcement with several roads being briefly closed as a result of flooding. The system also produced strong wind gusts across the area between the afternoon of December 30 and the morning of January 1 with several stations in the West Side Hills and Tehachapi Mountains reporting gusts exceeding 60 mph. Several stations in the Sierra Nevada below 7500 feet picked up between 4 and 7 inches of rainfall while the adjacent foothills picked up 2 to 4 inches of rainfall. Rain shadowing effects limited precipitation in the San Joaquin Valley to between half an inch and an inch of rain at most locations while many stations in the Tehachapi Mountains also picked up between half an inch and an inch of rain. Several higher elevations SNOTEL stations picked up 18 to 30 inches of new snowfall adding to the heavy snowpack which had already accumulated earlier in December.
episodes.175238: A winter storm produced significant snow in the higher elevations of southeast Arizona. Rain and strong winds affected the valleys. A few thunderstorms also occurred across Pima and Pinal counties. One storm downed a tree causing significant damage to a residence in Marana.
episodes.176175: A long wave trough moved across Arizona on on New Year's Day with bringing widespread precipitation. Snow levels were initially relatively high for this time of the year.  The snow levels dropped rapidly as a cold front associated with the trough moved across the area. The heavy rain and rain on snow caused flooding in the lower elevations.
episodes.176438: The strongest winter storm of December finished up early on New Year's day.  This atmospheric river (AR) enhanced winter storm initially produced very high snow levels near 9000 feet on 30 December with heavy rainfall continuing below that elevation.  But colder air and enhanced forcing, coupled with the final push of extensive moisture worked in unison to rapidly drop snow levels to most valley floors (above 4000 feet) during the morning of New Year���s Eve that carried over into the overnight hours through early morning New Year���s day. Some foothill areas received 1-2 feet plus of new snow with Sierra snowfall totals generally ranging from 18-30 inches below 7000 feet. Higher Sierra areas and passes received 3-4 feet plus of accumulating snow above 7000 feet before the winter system exited the region.
episodes.176842: A strong winter storm starting in late December 2022 carried over into January 2023, bringing heavy rain and mountain snow to southern California.
episodes.176926: A strong winter storm brought widespread snowfall and winter impacts to much of the forecast region for the start of 2023. Some of the high elevation locations saw snow begin prior to the new year, while most valley locations saw rain switch to snow right around midnight on the new year. Additionally, isolated flash flooding was reported in southern Utah due to rainfall associated with the system.
episodes.177003: A strong atmospheric storm brought moderate to heavy rain and a period of strong winds New Years Eve into early New Years Day, along with heavy high-elevation Sierra snow. There were 3 fatalities reported due to drowning. Precipitation totals by 8 am (over 24 hours) were around 1 to 3 inches for the southern Sacramento and northern San Joaquin Valleys, 3 to 8 inches for the Motherlode foothills and Northern Sierra from around SR 70 southward, with widespread flooding in those areas. Rainfall further north was generally an inch or less. There was significant river flooding on the Cosumnes River in Sacramento County around Wilton, due to multiple levee breaks. The river reached flood stage on the morning of December 31, and stayed in flood stage past midnight and into January 1. The flooding resulted in the evacuation of Wilton as the river went out-of-bank, with area highways and roads being closed, including SR-99. Significant flooding occurred from Wilton downstream through Interstate 5. River flooding was also reported along the Mokelumne River near Benson's Ferry and Mormon Slough at Bellota. Flooding of streams, in low areas and from clogged storm drains also closed many other roads across Northern California, with several small communities being evacuated. These events occurred mainly on December 31st and were reported on that date. Heavy snow disrupted mountain travel, with a total of 20 to 40 inches of snow above 6000 feet by the morning of the 1st. There were multiple spinouts causing Interstate 80 to be shut down for 18 hours. Highway 50 was closed in El Dorado County due to a combination of flooding and snow. High winds gusting to 50-65 mph in the Central Valley caused large numbers of trees to fall, bringing widespread power failures across the area, with hundreds of thousands of customers impacted. Most of the strong winds occurred on New Years Eve, with the damage events being reported on December 31, 2022, but power outage issues continued for tens of thousands of customers into the new year. Many local roads were also closed to downed trees blocking them, as well as many trees were reported to have fallen on homes and automobiles.
episodes.177077: An ice jam developed along the Penobscot River during the afternoon of December 27th near Howland...which persisted into the morning of the 1st. The ice jam led to minor flooding in the vicinity of Merrill Brook Lane and Garden Lane. The flooding impacted a low lying bridge which cut off access to several residents on an island. Rising waters behind the ice jam also eventually impacted Mattamiscontis Road near Gordon Brook. A water rescue was required due  to a vehicle being driven into the flood waters and stalling. No injuries occurred. The ice jam eventually reached 2 to 3 miles in length. The ice jam released during the morning of the 1st allowing river levels to fall.
episodes.177450: A series of atmospheric river systems impacted Interior Northern California and produced substantial flooding and wind damage.

CalTrans report of flooding in the right lane on I-5 South near Oceanside.
Public report of flooding on SR78 West on the on-ramp to I-5 North.

Heavy rain fell across much of San Diego County on January 1st. Per reports from NWS Employees and other trained spotters rainfall totals of 1-3 inches fell across much of the county through the evening hours on the 1st.
A trained spotter reported storm total rainfall of 1.4 inches through about 8 AM.
A trained spotter reported 1.78 inches of heavy rain occurring at their location through about 8 AM on the 1st.

The Cosumnes River rose rapidly due to very heavy rains and already elevated levels from previous storms. Sacramento County OES confirmed the levee along the Cosumnes River breached in three locations overnight, causing flash flooding in the surrounding areas from Rancho Murieta to Wilton. SR 99 between Dillard Rd and Grantline Rd was flooded with numerous vehicles stuck in flood waters, requiring water rescues and was closed around midnight due to flooding. Flooding continued well into January. Sacramento County issued an evacuation warning overnight for the Wilton area, changed to a shelter-in-place warning a couple of hours later due to unsafe travel conditions with surrounding flooded areas. There were an estimated 3,200 to 3,500 people in the impacted area. There were three drownings attributed to the flooding, each entered as an individual event.

Sacramento County completed a preliminary estimate of a total of $133 million from public storm damage from January 1 through January 17, and a total of almost $700,000 in private property damage. There was extensive levee damage and flooding along the Cosumnes River from Rancho Murieta to Wilton. There was also widespread flooding of streams, creeks, and roadways across the county. Large numbers of trees were reported down from strong wind events, with widespread power outages and reports of damage to homes and cars.

Colusa County completed a preliminary estimate of damage to roads, road closures, debris removal, and high river levels of about $800,000 in damage. The Colusa Boat Landing had some damages to the private levee, with an estimate of about $200,000.

Glenn County completed a preliminary estimate of damage from flooding. There was substantial flooding, resulting in the closure of more than 25 roads. There was over $5 million in damage to public infrastructure. There was significant bank erosion on a number of major creeks, stream, and the Sacramento River.

San Joaquin County completed a preliminary estimate of damage from flooding. There was substantial flooding, with around $24.7million in individual assistance/private property loss including 172 properties destroyed and 194 properties with major damage. There was around $82 million in public damages. The estimated grand total as of January 26 was $106.9 million.

Tehama County completed a preliminary estimate of damage from flooding. There was substantial flooding, with a rough estimate of $14 million in damages, mainly from 3 bridges, 1 completely destroyed by under cutting, two others under cut and sink holes, but still standing. Kirkwood Bridge $6,110,000.00 , Rawson Bridge $4,000,000.00. Remainder in trees, bridge clearing, road damage, labor $4,000,000.00||The city of Red Bluff estimated $60,000.00 bridge, trees, sandbags, labor (still climbing as they find more). The city of Corning estimated $100,000.00 road damage, creek and bridge clearing and labor. The city of Tehama estimated $27,000.00 road damage to East Gyle, tree clean up and debris clean up from roads.
Yolo County completed a preliminary estimate of damage from flooding, which is around $11 million in damages for the county and its partners.

Mesonet station (LOBC1-SNOTEL) located 8.4 mi S of Walker, CA and mesonet station (SRAC1-SNOTEL) located 2.0 mi SE of Sonora Pass, CA reported 24 hour heavy rainfall totals of 3.6 and 3.4 inches  respectively during the period from 12/31/22 through 1/1/23.

COCORAHS Station (CA-NV-51) located 2.0 mi N Truckee, CA, and CO-OP observer located 1.0 mi SSW of Boca Reservoir, CA, reported 24 hour heavy rainfall totals of 5.57 and 4.62 inches respectively during the period from 12/31/22 through 1/1/23.
COCORAHS  Station (CA-ED-20) located 2.0 mi NW of Meyers, CA, reported 24 hour heavy rainfall totals of 8.32 inches during the period from 12/31/22 through 1/1/23.
California Highway Patrol reported closing the mouth of Kern Canyon with two sections of large boulders blocking the eastbound lanes of SR 178 near NM 17 and NM 21.
California Highway Patrol reported a few feet of mud on part of SR 41 near Tenaya Lodge in Oakhurst.
California Highway Patrol reported rocks washed up on the roadway at the intersection of N. Piedra Rd. and Elwood Rd.

Flash flooding on College Avenue near SR76 reported by CalTrans. Full highway closure with disabled vehicles due to water up to 2.5 feet deep. Rainfall rates of 0.84 inch per hour occurred in the area, per observations from KCRQ ASOS.
Public report of flooding on SR76 at I-5. Water was reported to be up to 2.5 feet deep.

The California Highway Patrol on January 4 reported a fatality associated with the December 31 - January 1 flash flood due to levee breaks. A female body was found outside a vehicle near Dillard Road east of CA-99. This is one of three confirmed fatalities from this event.
Flooding reported in all lanes on SR94 West at College Ave. A vehicle was stuck and flooded out on the right shoulder.
US Military Police reported roadway flooding at the intersection of S. Dickenson Ave. and W. Oakland Ave. at Lemoore Naval Air Station.
California Highway Patrol reported rocks washed up on the road at the intersection of SR 198 and SR 216 in Lemoncove.
California Highway Patrol reported a tree washed up on the roadway on SR 168.
California Highway Patrol reported a tree blocking the roadway on Rd. 426 near Rd. 222. at Bass Lake.
California Highway Patrol reported roadway flooding at the intersection of SR 59 and McNamara Rd.
CalTrans report of flooding on the Mount Soledad Freeway near the I-15 on-ramp.
CalTrans report of flooding on the Palm Ave off-ramp lanes on I-5 in Imperial Beach.
CalTrans report of flooding on the Palm Ave off-ramp lanes on I-5 near Imperial Beach.

Sacramento County Sheriff confirmed a drowning on January 4 associated with the December 31 - January 1 flash flood event. A female body was found inside a vehicle. This was the third drowning associated with the event. This flooding was due to levee breaks on the Cosumnes River.
CalTrans report of a mudslide leading to rocks and dirt blocking eastbound lanes on Via de Santa Fe near Rancho Santa Fe.
CalTrans report of a mudslide on Old Julian Highway by MM 4.5.
California Highway Patrol reported a tree blocking part of the intersection of SR 168 and Tollhouse Rd.
Associated with persistent ongoing moderate to heavy rain, park rangers at Zion National Park reported several canyons around the park were flooding.

Per an NWS Storm Survey, levels on the San Diego River at Fashion Valley reached up to 10.2 feet. Fashion Valley Road had 1 foot of flowing water and was closed. Avenida Del Rio had 2 feet of flowing water and was closed. The entire lower parking structure at the Fashion Valley Mall was filled with 1 to 2 feet of water. Mission Center Road was closed but did not have flowing water. Riverwalk Golf Driving Range was filled with water. San Diego Mission Road had minor water flow debris at crossing, but was open.

Oak Creek began to rise at the river gauge in Sedona 1100 AM on January 1 (550 CFS), crested at over 4,500 CFC at around 500 PM (a 4 foot rise), and then returned to near normal by 1100 AM on January 2.  The Oak Creek gauge near Cornville began to rise at 400 PM on January 1 (440 CFS), crested at over 4,000 CFC in the action stage at around 900 PM (a 4.9 foot rise), and then returned to near normal after 500 PM on January 2. A video on social media showed flooding of low water crossings on Oak Creek near Rainbow Mobile Home Park and The Rainbow Trout Farm.
California Highway Patrol reported a large boulder blocking both lanes of Jose Basin Rd. near the intersection with Sugarloaf Rd.
California Highway Patrol reported roadway flooding on Buchanan Hallow Rd. south of LeGrand.

There was a male fatality due to drowning in a submerged car, confirmed by Cosumnes Fire Department near SR 99 and Dillard Rd. A levee breech on the Cosumnes River caused the flash flood. This was one of three drowning deaths reported from the flash flood event. The Cosumnes Fire Department said they rescued dozens of people in the area over the past 24 hours. A helicopter from Metro Fire also rescued several people in the area. SR 99 remained closed due to flooding on the roadway. Several vehicles are still stuck in the flood waters. Wilton firefighters responded to 25 vehicles stranded in flood water and half a dozen fallen power lines. They also cleared many downed trees from the roadways as they navigated around Wilton.
California Highway Patrol reported water from a canal flooding onto the roadway south of Merced.

Associated with persistent ongoing moderate to at times heavy rain, local law enforcement reported flash flooding in Snow Canyon State Park, including water moving over Snow Canyon Road which made the road impassable. The flooding also necessitated the closure of the south entrance to the park.

Rainfall rates of 0.5 to 0.8 inches per hour were observed in this area between 4 and 5 PM. Total rainfall of 1.30 inches occurred just west of Cranston Station near Valle Vista at Blackburn Road and State Highway 74. Flooding occurred at this location around 2:30 PM as well.
Thunderstorm winds downed a shallow-rooted tree which fell onto a mobile home, causing significant roof and wall damage.
